title: Match Substring After Replacement
summary: Given the strings s and sub, along with a 2D character array mappings where mappings[i] = [oldi, newi] indicates that you can replace the character oldi in sub with newi any number of times (with each character in sub being replaced at most once), determine whether it is possible to transform sub into a substring of s through these replacements.
statement: Given the strings s and sub, along with a 2D character array mappings where mappings[i] = [oldi, newi] indicates that you can replace the character oldi in sub with newi any number of times (with each character in sub being replaced at most once), determine whether it is possible to transform sub into a substring of s through these replacements. If so, return true; otherwise, return false. A substring is defined as a contiguous non-empty sequence of characters within a string.
constraints: Each mapping [old,new] permits one occurrence of old in sub to become new; unchanged characters are always allowed.
Each pattern position may be replaced at most once and mappings are directional.
Return whether some transformed sub equals a contiguous substring of s.
hints: Store allowed directional character pairs in a set.
For each possible source-window start, compare corresponding characters independently.
A position matches when characters are equal or (sub_char,source_char) is allowed; accept when all positions match.
Every valid transformation acts independently at each position, so the window predicate is necessary and sufficient, and all windows are tested.
editorial: Every valid transformation acts independently at each position, so the window predicate is necessary and sufficient, and all windows are tested.
